title: 1971 AHSME Problem 28
statement: Nine lines parallel to the base of a triangle divide the other sides each into \(10\) equal segments and the area into \(10\) distinct parts. If the area of the largest of these parts is \(38,\) then the area of the original triangle is:

solutions.text:
If the whole area is \(K,\) the triangle above the bottom strip is similar to the original with scale \(\frac{9}{10},\) so its area is \(\frac{81K}{100}.\) Thus the largest strip has area \[ K-\frac{81K}{100}=\frac{19K}{100}=38, \] giving \(K=200.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: The largest part is the bottom strip
The smaller triangle above that strip has linear scale \(\frac{9}{10}\)
